page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring a single dedicated vCPU based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the single-core CPU performance is in the average tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0. However, because it features only one physical core and one thread, multi-core performance scales identically to single-core, placing it in the lower tier for multi-threaded workloads. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read speeds of 11.99 GB/sec and write speeds of 7.95 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware-accelerated AES support, though other advanced instruction sets like AVX or AMX are absent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a low-overhead entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, offering dedicated CPU resources without the shared-core performance degradation of burstable instances. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale Redis caching, development environments, and simple utility scripts that do not require high memory bandwidth or parallel processing capabilities.
